evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run a program in Zambia where community health agents sell condoms door to door. We are adding five work-motivation items to the quarterly agent survey, which supervisors read aloud in Bemba (Copperbelt) and Nyanja (Lusaka). English items: (1) In the last month, how often did you feel proud of your work as an agent? never / sometimes / often / always. (2) How much do people in your community respect the work you do? not at all / a little / a lot. (3) In the last month, how many times did someone refuse to talk to you because of what you sell? (number). (4) If you could, would you keep doing this work next year? no / not sure / yes. (5) How fair is the commission you earn for what you do? not fair / somewhat fair / fair. They measure pride (1), perceived respect (2), stigma exposure (3), intention to continue (4), and fairness of pay (5). Not a published scale. We have two program officers who are native Bemba speakers, one Nyanja-speaking supervisor from Lusaka, and an M&E lead who knows the constructs and reads both languages. We can hold a half-day meeting. No donor requirement for back-translation. Nothing is translated yet. Set this up for us.
evals.expected_output: A translation record in the output template with the brief, the team, and the back-translation decision filled in, and the translations marked pending.
assertions: Sorts each of the five items as close translation, adapt, or concept in doubt, with something to watch for.
Names two translators working apart for Bemba and says Nyanja has only one fluent speaker available.
States a back-translation decision and the reason for it.
Does not present Bemba or Nyanja wording of its own as the final translation.
Lists items to test with respondents and says the translation is untested until then.
Does not reword the English items or call the result validated.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Can you translate our survey into Swahili?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the items, the variety of Swahili and how the survey is given, what each item measures, and who is available, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the source items word for word.
Asks which variety of Swahili, or where the survey will run.
Asks what each item is meant to measure.
Asks who is available to translate or review.
Does not produce any Swahili text.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We are a maternal health NGO in Amhara, Ethiopia. We want the PHQ-9 in Amharic so that health extension workers can screen mothers at postnatal visits and refer anyone scoring 10 or above to the district counselor. Items are the standard nine with 'not at all / several days / more than half the days / nearly every day', each measuring a depression symptom over the last two weeks. We don't know of an existing Amharic version. Respondents are rural mothers, many with no schooling; items are read aloud. We have an Amharic-speaking psychiatric nurse, two bilingual program officers, and a health extension worker who can join a meeting. Translate it.
evals.expected_output: The skill sets up the translation and says a psychometrician or clinical researcher must be consulted, because the cut-off of 10 does not carry over to a translated screener.
assertions: Fills in the brief and names who translates, who reviews, and who adjudicates.
Says the cut-off of 10 does not carry over to the translation, or needs local validation.
Names a psychometrician, clinician, or clinical researcher to consult.
Says what to bring to that specialist.
Tells the user to look for an existing tested Amharic version.
Does not call the Amharic version validated.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our Chichewa questionnaire for pregnant women in Mchinji is already translated and the team is happy with it. Can you check whether the women will actually understand it? We can interview ten of them next week.
evals.expected_output: The skill says the translation exists and the need is to test whether respondents understand it, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the translation is already done, so nothing needs translating.
Names draft-cognitive-interview-script.
Does not produce a translation record.
